PCI.BIO: Dr. Sanjeev Kumar is a professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering. He is active in teaching & research in the area of Digital Systems Engineering, Computer Network Security, Wireless Security, High-Speed Internet Switching/Routing, and Computer Architecture. Before joining UTPA, Dr. Kumar worked with the leading networking companies in the United States. He has authored over 60 technical papers, book, book chapters, and several patents. He received the Ph.D. degree from Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering with emphasis on Computer Engineering, North Carolina State University, Raleigh, North Carolina.  He is the founder of NSF funded Network Security Research Lab (NRL) in Electrical & Computer Engineering Department. He has supervised & graduated one of the highest number of Thesis students in the department and many of his students are now working at computer and networking companies. He is a winner of UT Systems Regents' Outstanding Teaching Award, and many UTPA Teaching Excellence Awards. He is an elected Senior member of IEEE.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: A Fast Implementation of the Rijndael Substitution Box for Cryptographic AES
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: Today's current standard in Cryptography is the symmetric Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) as selected by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). It is also known as Rijndael Encryption Algorithm. With the emergence of high-performance cloud computing, it is important for the security encryption schemes to perform at higher speeds to provide fast, efficient, and secure data transmissions. The Rijndael S-box (substitution box) is the only non-linear component of the cryptosystem and significantly affects the overall performance of the AES encryption scheme. In this paper, we investigate various implementations for improving the hardware performance of the Rijndael S-box component of the AES algorithm in terms of delay and number of logic elements on the Altera Cyclone IV FPGA (Field programmable gate arrays) using the Intel Quartus II software and Verilog Hardware Description Language (Verilog HDL).

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Effect of Intermediate Network Systems on Remote Power Data Collection in Smart Grid
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: This paper investigates impact of intermediate switches on remote collection of power consumption data in Smart Grid. Advance metering infrastructure (AMI) is one of the important components in the overall architecture of the Smart Grid. Implementation of AMI has been a topic of research lately as there are many different implementations being used in today's Smart Grid. One of the AMI network is Ethernet based infrastructure for the access of remote power consumption from the customer premises. In this paper, we are investigating impact of Ethernet switches on the power consumption data reported to the utility companies. This paper investigates the impact on the customer power consumption by utilizing commonly used Ethernet switches from different companies. Power consumption data in the presence of Ethernet switch is compared with the baseline Power consumption data when no switches were used. Experimental work as discussed in this paper shows a clear impact on customer power consumption due to the Ethernet based Advanced Metering Infrastructure.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Evaluation of CentOS performance under IoT based DDoS Security Attacks
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: The increasing interest in `always-connected' devices and the Internet of Things (IoT) technologies have led to many electronic devices with Internet connectivity becoming omnipresent in modern households and workplaces. Consequently, this increase has also led to an increase in vulnerable IoT devices, ripe for being hijacked by a malicious third party. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks have consistently been an issue since the birth of the Internet. With the large number of IoT devices available today, the strength and intensity of these attacks continue to grow. Not all devices are created equal in terms of vulnerabilities that may exist with them. Many harbor flaws that allow them to be used as a bot by an external malicious host without the knowledge of the owner. Myriad of such devices can be used in a network of zombie machines (botnet) meant to carry out an attack. These botnets are used to flood a victim system with information aimed at consuming large amounts of resources, such as memory or processing power. In this paper, we evaluated the performance of CentOS 15 operating system under four popular DDoS attack scenarios in a controlled experimental environment.

INTELLCONT.TITLE: Evaluation of Internet Connectivity Under Distributed Denial of Service Attacks from Botnets of Varying Magnitudes
INTELLCONT.PUBLISHER: IEEE International Conference on Data Intelligence and Security (ICDIS)
INTELLCONT.ABSTRACT: In the last decade, electronic devices with internet accessibility have become commonplace. With the consistent growth and evolution of the Internet, Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks are increasingly more common and sophisticated. These attacks, depending on their type and magnitude, can be devastating to system intended to be the target of said attack. Several compromised internet-connected computer systems become part of a Botnet which can perform small to large scale DDoS attacks causing the victim system to consume resources, such as bandwidth, memory or processing power, at an alarming rate. With no available resources to process information, legitimate connections are unable to access the system under attack hence affecting operations related to the targeted system. In this paper, we study and analyze two common DDoS attacks using a set of simulated networks containing a range of over 16 million systems, 65 thousand systems and 254 systems against a targeted system in a closed lab environment as legitimate traffic attempts to reach the targeted system.

PRESENT.ABSTRACT:
In today’s society, most home security systems are overpriced due to the fact that they are monitored by a
home security system company. We are proposing a system that offers motion detection and other valuable
functions such as CO detection, live video. It will alert users in case of emergency by sending automated
notifications of security violations. This will be controlled by an Android application, eliminating the need of a
monitoring service company and it will make the user the main and primary contact in case of an emergency. This
low-cost security system will be created for indoor use only and it can be placed in a compact area around the house.

SERVICE_PUBLIC.ORG: Research Experiences for High School Students - Outreach Activities
SERVICE_PUBLIC.DESC:
Mentoring High School Students for High Scholar summer research.

Description: Working with High School Students during the summer time is an excellent and a meaningful outreach activity that directly influences the students' decision to join UTRGV after their graduation from High School. In Summer of 2020, I mentored 3 High School Students for their participation in Summer research at the Cyber Security Research Lab in the College of Engineering and Computer Science at UTRGV for 10 weeks of Summer. High School Students were trained initially for their participation in research activities in the lab. Students were given problems to investigate and provide their findings to the research group and make presentations during weekly meetings. They also made final poster presentations to compete in a university wide contest at the end of the High Scholar program. At the contest, students poster presentations were evaluated.
To me this is a great outreach opportunity to work with the High School students and help improve the stature of the UTRGV. These students are the future undergraduate students who would feel confident coming to UTRGV to seek further education after their graduation from High School.
SERVICE_PUBLIC.ACCOMPLISH: Three High School Students participated in High Scholar Summer Research in the Cyber Security Research Lab under my mentorship. The High School students learned new technologies and skills in computer security. The Mentored High School Students made poster presentations at the High Scholar program.
